title: Cross-team dependability assembly: 30-60-120 plan and experiment manifest
content:
Purpose:
This is a working plan + experiment manifest to assemble a small cross-functional cohort (service owners + infra + product) to define, instrument, and operationalize SLOs for a set of medium-risk model-serving paths. Goal is to validate a repeatable 30-60-120 runbook that teams can adopt with minimal SRE coaching.

Scope (what's IN):
- 3 pilot services (model routing, cache tier, streaming API) identified by PLT and SRE.
- Define 1 primary and 1 secondary SLO per service (availability and end-to-end latency).
- Instrument metrics, alerts, and an initial error-budget policy.
- Run 30/60/120 day experiments to refine thresholds and response workflows.

Scope (what's OUT):
- Full org-wide rollout (this is a cohort pilot).
- Deep architectural changes to runtime (we will note blockers).

Success criteria (how we'll know the cohort worked):
- Each pilot service has a documented SLO and an automated telemetry dashboard within 60 days.
- Alert noise reduced to <3 actionable paging events per week per service during the 60-day observation window.
- Two guardrail improvements implemented (e.g., KV cache TTL tuning, fallback model variant) and validated by experiment.
- Runbook template accepted by Product and Platform leads.

High-level timeline (30 / 60 / 120 cadence)
- Day 0-30 (Discovery + Fast Instrument):
  - Kickoff workshop with service owners, product manager, SRE partner, infra lead.
  - Baseline collection: collect 30 days of traffic/latency/error distribution from existing dashboards.
  - Draft SLOs and measurement windows (proposal templates below).
  - Lightweight instrumentation tickets created and owner assigned.
  - Quick experiments: enable a 1% canary routing to a cached path for latency comparison.
- Day 31-60 (Stabilize + Automate):
  - Dashboards and alerting wired to PagerDuty integration; runbook skeleton created.
  - Begin enforcement experiments (error budget burn simulation via traffic shaping in staging).
  - Postmortem playbook defined: how to treat SLO breaches vs. incidents.
  - Stakeholder retrospective at Day 60 to decide 120-day goals.
- Day 61-120 (Operationalize + Scale):
  - Harden automation (auto-rollbacks, fallback variants, circuit-breakers templates).
  - Oncall drills (tabletop + real 1-week oncall shadow) to validate runbooks.
  - Prepare adoption kit (templates, sample Jira board, Confluence how-to).
  - Decision: promote cohort pattern to broader teams or re-run with adjusted metrics.

SLO design template (fill-in):
- Service name: <service>
- User-visible indicator: <api-requests-success / p99-latency / embeddings-reply-time>
- SLO type: Availability | Latency | Freshness
- SLO target: e.g., 99.5% over 30d (availability), p95 < 120ms over 14d (latency)
- Measurement window: 30d | 14d | 7d (pick based on traffic patterns)
- Error budget policy: what counts as "error" (5xx, 429, tail latency > threshold), consumption rules, mitigation steps.
- Owner: service-frontend@, infra-pager-duty@, product-sponsor@

Minimal telemetry checklist (must be automated to pass Day60 gate):
- Metric: request_total, error_total (5xx+4xx if relevant), latency_histogram (p50/p95/p99).
- Labels: model_version, region, route, cache_hit=true/false.
- Dashboards: SLO burn rate, discrete error sources, request distribution.
- Alerts: SLO burn rate > 5x for 10m (warning), burn rate > 10x for 5m (critical).
- Log links: example trace id for typical error flows.

Runbook quick checklist (for each service):
- Triage owner assigned and reachable.
- Primary mitigation actions documented (scaled fallback, reroute, throttle).
- Rollback criteria and steps.
- Post-breach immediate actions and postmortem timeline.

Experiment manifest (per pilot service):
- Experiment name: cache-tier-latency-burst-compare
  - Hypothesis: enabling a small per-customer in-memory cache reduces p95 latency by >=20% during peak.
  - Variants: baseline vs 10% traffic via cache.
  - Metrics tracked: p50/p95/p99 latency, cache hit ratio, CPU/GPU load, error rate.
  - Success criteria: p95 reduction >= 15% and no increase in error rate beyond 0.1% absolute.
  - Rollback triggers: error rate > 0.5% absolute or CPU saturation > 85% sustained for 5m.

Stakeholders and roles (first cohort):
- SRE lead (Rafael Chen) - shepherd instrumentation and alert tuning.
- Service owners: model-routing (Priya Nair), streaming-api (Jonah Lee), cache-service (Asha Kumar).
- Product sponsor: Elena Park - customer impact prioritization.
- Infra/Platform: Maya Townsend - capacity policies and canary tooling.
- Observability eng: Siva Menon - dashboarding and log/trace collection.

Communication plan:
- Weekly sync: 30-min on Tuesdays (status + blockers).
- Slack channel: #sre-dependability-cohort (use threads for experiments).
- Office hours: SRE office hours Thursday 1-2p for quick unblock.
- Stakeholder reviews: Day 30 and Day 60 demos (20m each).

Risks and early mitigations:
- Risk: metric cardinality explosion from labels.
  - Mitigation: enforce low-cardinality label set in initial schema; sample more detailed logs to separate storage.
- Risk: noisy alerts during ramp.
  - Mitigation: start with non-paging Slack warnings for first 2 weeks; tune thresholds before paging.
- Risk: product pushback on strict SLO targets.
  - Mitigation: use canary windows and experiment evidence to align targets with UX impact.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide final measurement windows for each service (30d vs 14d) -> ACTION: Priya to propose by 2026-02-18.
- Confirm PagerDuty escalation policy mapping for cohort -> ACTION: Rafael to file JIRA-SRE-2117-subtask.
- Confirm data retention / cost tradeoffs for histogram buckets -> ACTION: Siva to estimate cost by 2026-02-22.

Templates to attach in Confluence (to author after Day 30):
- SLO definition form (fields + examples).
- Runbook template with checklists.
- Experiment runbook template (hypothesis, variant config, metric probes, rollback).

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc intentionally lightweight — the value is in the working experiments and artifacts.
- Emphasize small wins (2 guardrail changes) over perfect SLO math in pilot.
- Expect changes to alert thresholds after real traffic experiments.

Appendix: example SLO wording (draft)
- Model routing availability SLO: "99.7% of requests routed to a healthy model variant complete with status 2xx within 1s over a 30-day rolling window."
- Streaming API latency SLO: "p95 end-to-end response time < 250ms over a 14-day window, for requests < 1k tokens."

Linked references / quick links:
- CONFL-5842-service-dependability-canvas (draft)
- JIRA-SRE-2117 (cohort kickoff epics)
- Runtime PR for canary tooling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412

End of working plan.

-- Maya
